parts.note: in cricket a paceman is a fast bowler

explanation.surface: A cricket team picks a second fast bowler and wonders whether a man called Armstrong might fit the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Armstrong reads like a cricketer's surname, but it is Neil Armstrong, first man on the Moon; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Armstrong was an astronaut, a traveller beyond Earth, which is what the answer means.

clue.text: Culinary skill shown by family filling container

indicators.note: the family word goes inside, filling up the container word

parts.note: a bag is a container
kin means family, relatives

explanation.surface: A cookery skill is demonstrated by a family stuffing a box.
explanation.definitionFit: Baking is the cooking art of making bread and cakes in an oven, a kitchen skill.

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering, so the remaining letters are jumbled
almost the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written; a local is also British slang for one's nearby pub

explanation.surface: At the pub a drink has nearly been finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims LOCAL to LOCA, and 'drunk' rearranges those letters. A 'local' is a Briton's neighbourhood pub, which makes the surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cola is a sweet fizzy soft drink flavoured originally with kola nut.

clue.text: Wasted header in box leading to draw

indicators.note: the header of a word is its top letter, here taken from the word box

parts.note: taken as written for its first letter
a lotto is a lottery, a prize draw

explanation.surface: A footballer's header into the box sets up a drawn match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'header' and 'box' sound like football, but the header is just the leading letter B of 'box'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for extremely drunk, so one can replace the other.

clue.text: Visible, person initially adopted by a mum or dad

indicators.note: taken in by, so the letter goes inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: either of these is a parent

indicators.note: the first letter of person

explanation.surface: A person is visibly adopted by a single parent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives P from 'person', which goes inside A PARENT, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means plainly seen or evident, a near synonym of visible.

parts.note: to charge a glass is to fill it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A ski lift costs one penny to ride.

explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a boost or stimulus, something that raises spirits, as a lift does.

clue.text: Prison sentence that is right, first of all

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the following four words

indicators.note: mixed up, so the letters of the two animals are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird, a wolf and an ape are confused with each other.

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Showcasing a particular nation.

clue.text: Vehicle connected, later I turned right

indicators.note: puzzling or confusing, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An enormous store is a puzzle on which almost everyone concurs.

explanation.definitionFit: The starling is a common speckled songbird known for its huge flocks.

indicators.note: the last letter of appetite

explanation.definitionFit: A pie is a baked dish with a pastry crust and filling.

indicators.note: bending twists things, so the letters are rearranged

indicators.note: dreadfully done, so the letters are jumbled

indicators.note: pressing into, so the dance word takes the other letters inside it

explanation.surface: A dance which impresses the boyfriend of a woman.

clue.text: A lot caught in tassel, door swinging up

the letters are caught inside the following words

indicators.note: built means constructed, so the letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A white church constructed by a man named Basil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' reads as the church's colour but defines a wine.

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.definitionFit: A head is a headland, a promontory jutting into the sea.

indicators.note: going back means reading the letters in reverse

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means
dim means dark

explanation.definitionFit: A midge is a tiny biting fly, a gnat.

indicators.note: reading aloud gives a sound-alike of the word

parts.note: letters are mail, the post

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: down is the opposite of up, so not up

clue.text: Source of crude painting, in all likelihood

parts.note: an oil is a painting in oils
well means probably, as in 'it may well rain'

explanation.surface: A rude picture is probably the source of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude' suggests vulgarity, but it is crude oil.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil well is a borehole that brings up petroleum, crude oil, from the ground.
